learning_objective: 🎯 You will discover the secret recipe of English sentence structure and learn how to arrange words and phrases so they make perfect sense!

key_vocabulary.hindi_meaning: कर्म (जिस पर काम हो रहा हो)

main_concepts.simple_explanation: English has a strict rule for basic sentences: Subject first, then Verb, then Object (S-V-O). For example, 'Rahul (Subject) kicked (Verb) the ball (Object).' If you mix the order and say 'The ball kicked Rahul', the whole meaning changes!

main_concepts.concept_title: 🧩 What is a Phrase? (The Missing Puzzle Piece)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: A Phrase is a group of words that work together to add meaning, but unlike a clause, it DOES NOT have a subject and a verb. Examples include 'in the morning' or 'the tall boy'. They are like extra decorations you add to your main sentence.

main_concepts.concept_title: ✨ Placing Modifiers Correctly (Don't Confuse the Reader!)
main_concepts.simple_explanation: Adjectives and adverbs are modifiers; they describe other words. You must keep them right next to the word they are describing. If you say 'I saw a man riding a horse with a broken leg', who has the broken leg? The man or the horse? Proper order fixes this!

Prepositional phrases start with words like in, on, at, under, or behind. They tell us WHERE or WHEN something happened. They usually go at the very end of the sentence or right at the beginning. Example: 'In the park, the kids played football.'

fun_activity.title: 🕵️‍♂️ The Jumbled Sentence Detective
fun_activity.instructions: Ask a friend or parent to write 3 long sentences, then chop them up into individual words. Try to rearrange them back into perfect S-V-O order using your new word order skills!

quick_recap: ⭐ The standard English word order is Subject + Verb + Object (S-V-O).
⭐ A phrase is a group of words that adds detail but lacks a subject-verb pair.
⭐ Keep describing words (modifiers) as close as possible to the words they describe.
⭐ Prepositional phrases help explain where or when an action takes place.
